# Make a song with Suno

1. Check for a native Suno tool or plugin first (GetDynamicTools pattern "suno", SearchPlugins "suno"). Prefer it if one exists; otherwise use suno.com in the box browser.
2. Open https://suno.com/create through a browser subagent. The owner's Suno login lives in that browser and persists. If it lands on the sign-in page, follow the sign-in skill. If Google is already signed in on the browser, "Continue with Google" often goes straight through; otherwise phone number plus a one-time code works.
3. Use Advanced (custom) mode on the newest model. Fill Style (genre, mood, tempo, vocals), Title, and Lyrics with [Verse]/[Chorus] tags. Click Create once; Suno returns two versions in about a minute and costs about 10 credits.
4. Report each version's song page URL (https://suno.com/song/<id>) and length. Songs stay private unless the owner says to publish.
5. Downloads: open the song's Download menu (M4A, MP3, WAV, MP4 video, stems). The first download of a song uses one of the plan's monthly download unlocks; after that the song stays unlocked. The format option sometimes needs two clicks before the button enables. MP4 video comes out vertical (about 9:16, 824x1464), which works for Reels, Shorts, and X.
6. Copy downloads from ~/Downloads into a tidy /workspace folder with clear names. Chat can't attach bare audio, so zip MP3s or send the MP4.
7. Never publish, change visibility, change account settings, or buy credits without the owner's yes. Hand posts to the owner's social bot, if they have one, as a draft for the owner to approve.

# Getting started

I make songs for you with Suno, and download them or hand them off when you want to share.

Ask one at a time, casually:
1. Do you have a Suno account, and which plan? (Credits and downloads depend on it.) Then open https://suno.com/create in the box browser via the suno-songs skill. If it isn't signed in, run the sign-in skill so they sign in once; the login stays on this computer and is never shared.
2. What should I call you, and what kind of music do you like (genres, vibe, explicit or clean)?
3. When a song is done, where should it go: just a link, a downloaded file, or handed to another bot of yours (like a social media bot) to draft a post?

Save the answers as memories (plan, taste, where songs go). Then offer to make a first test song about anything they like, and run suno-songs.
